articles.title: 5 dicas para proteger o seu pescoço do estresse e da má postura | G1
articles.standfirst: O mundo moderno é um desafio para o nosso pescoço, mas há muitas coisas que podemos fazer para reduzir o risco de desenvolver problemas.
articles.summary: O mundo moderno é um desafio para o nosso pescoço, mas há muitas coisas que podemos fazer para reduzir o risco de desenvolver problemas.
articles.body:
A vida moderna, incluindo o uso frequente de celulares e laptops, é péssima para o nosso pescoço — Foto: BBC / Getty Imagens

Às vezes, é preciso pensar sobre o peso da cabeça humana.

Quando estamos sentados ou em pé, com o corpo ereto, a carga mecânica que a cabeça exerce sobre o pescoço é de apenas cerca 5,4 kg, explica Anthony Ghosh, neurocirurgião especializado em coluna do Serviço Nacional de Saúde do Reino Unido (NHS), no Queen's Hospital, em Londres. Isso não é um problema.

Mas, em todo o mundo, bilhões de pessoas passam grande parte do dia com o corpo curvado para a frente. E, à medida que nos inclinamos sobre nossos laptops e smartphones, alteramos radicalmente a distribuição do peso sobre o pescoço.

Nessa posição desconfortável, olhando para baixo, a carga que a cabeça exerce sobre o pescoço aumenta para cerca de 27 kg, afirma Ghosh. "É uma sobrecarga considerável que o pescoço precisa suportar."

Em resumo, a vida moderna é péssima para o nosso pescoço. Mas há cinco dicas simples que você pode seguir para manter o pescoço saudável e prevenir problemas no futuro, independentemente da sua idade.

Alguns problemas no pescoço são uma consequência natural das mudanças que ocorrem em nosso sistema musculoesquelético à medida que envelhecemos, resultando em uma redução da elasticidade e em um aumento da rigidez dos tecidos que dão suporte ao pescoço. Embora esse tipo de desgaste não possa ser totalmente evitado, os exercícios podem ajudar a retardar esse processo.

"Ninguém com mais de 40 anos tem uma ressonância magnética da coluna completamente normal", afirma Ghosh. "Todo mundo terá algum desgaste nos discos, que são as estruturas que funcionam como uma espécie de amortecedor entre as vértebras. As articulações na parte posterior do pescoço também ficam um pouco mais espessas e rígidas."

Há ainda o impacto da tecnologia. Quando nos debruçamos sobre dispositivos eletrônicos, adotamos uma postura característica, com o pescoço inclinado para a frente. A parte superior das costas se curva, formando uma postura excessivamente encurvada, enquanto o queixo e a cabeça se projetam para a frente, em vez de ficarem alinhados diretamente sobre os ombros. Isso exerce uma grande pressão tanto sobre os músculos do pescoço quanto sobre as articulações das vértebras na parte superior da coluna.

Segundo uma análise do relatório Global Burden of Disease 2021, entre 60% e 80% das pessoas terão dores no pescoço ao longo da vida, e quase 50% delas enfrentarão o problema de forma frequente ou recorrente.

Esses problemas podem começar com uma sensação cada vez maior de rigidez e perda de mobilidade na parte superior da coluna, seguida por níveis crescentes e persistentes de desconforto.

De forma preocupante, pesquisas sugerem que problemas relacionados ao pescoço e à parte superior das costas estão começando a surgir mais cedo na vida.

A prevalência da escoliose aumentou de forma constante entre crianças e adolescentes nas últimas três décadas, segundo uma meta-análise de dados globais publicada em 2025.

Essa condição médica envolve o desenvolvimento de uma curvatura anormal da coluna, fazendo com que os músculos do pescoço precisem se esforçar e compensar para manter a cabeça nivelada.

Embora a causa da maioria dos casos de escoliose seja desconhecida, o estudo de 2025 encontrou uma associação significativa da condição com a má postura, o tempo prolongado sentado e o uso excessivo de telas, além de fatores como histórico familiar, sexo e baixo índice de massa corporal (IMC).

Mas há muitas coisas que podemos fazer para reduzir o risco de desenvolver problemas no pescoço.

Em vez de investir em cadeiras especiais ou outros recursos ergonômicos, Ghosh recomenda simplesmente se movimentar mais e fazer mais pausas durante o uso de telas. "A coluna simplesmente precisa se movimentar", afirma. "Isso faz com que a circulação flua por ela e ajuda a fortalecer os músculos."

Em particular, os exercícios a seguir podem ajudar a soltar as articulações, corrigir a má postura e tornar os músculos do pescoço mais resistentes aos efeitos de passar longos períodos olhando para a frente, em direção a uma tela.

Consulte sempre seu médico antes de iniciar uma nova rotina de exercícios.

Fazer pausas suficientes durante o uso do laptop pode ajudar a manter o pescoço em movimento e saudável — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Se você estiver sentindo dores no pescoço, o NHS (serviço de saúde pública do Reino Unido) recomenda um exercício simples para ajudar a recuperar a força e a mobilidade. Sentado com a postura ereta ou deitado de costas, vire a cabeça o máximo que conseguir para a direita e mantenha a posição por dois segundos.

Você deve sentir um alongamento no lado oposto do pescoço. Volte à posição inicial e, em seguida, vire a cabeça o máximo que conseguir para a esquerda. Repita o movimento duas ou três vezes , e faça o exercício ao longo do dia sempre que se sentir confortável.

Manter uma boa postura do pescoço é muito importante, pois a má postura sobrecarrega os músculos da região. Nosso pescoço foi feito para se movimentar em todas as direções, por isso uma dica é movimentá-lo regularmente ao longo do dia.

No entanto, a posição "ideal" para o pescoço é neutra, alinhada à coluna. Mantenha os ombros e as costas relaxados e o pescoço alongado e ereto. Tente evitar projetar o queixo para a frente e curvar os ombros, assim como permanecer por longos períodos com a cabeça inclinada ou virada para um dos lados.

Adotar essa postura é especialmente importante quando passamos muito tempo sentados, como ao trabalhar no computador, assistir televisão ou dirigir.

3. Corrija a postura do 'queixo projetado para a frente'

Passar anos olhando para a tela do computador pode levar à postura do "queixo projetado para a frente", em que a cabeça fica inclinada para a frente, em vez de alinhada com os ombros. No entanto, isso pode ser corrigido mudando alguns hábitos ao se sentar e fazendo exercícios simples.

Uma coisa que você pode fazer é alongar suavemente o pescoço para cima enquanto recolhe o queixo.

Imagine que há um pêssego macio sob o seu queixo. Você não quer amassá-lo recolhendo o queixo com muita força, mas também não deve deixá-lo cair.

Afaste suavemente as clavículas e puxe as escápulas para baixo e para trás, em direção ao centro da coluna. Ao mesmo tempo, contraia suavemente os músculos mais profundos do abdômen para manter a curvatura natural da região lombar.

Antes da industrialização, estudiosos passavam muitas horas debruçados sobre manuscritos. Mas Ghosh observou, em representações presentes em pinturas, que eles costumavam ler e escrever em estantes ou mesas inclinadas em cerca de 45 graus. Essa posição exercia menos pressão sobre o pescoço.

"As mesas inclinadas foram comuns durante séculos, pois eram mais adequadas ao uso de penas que eram mergulhadas em tinta", afirma Ghosh. Ele explica que, quando o papel ficava na horizontal, a tinta tinha mais dificuldade para secar e borrava com mais facilidade.

As mesas planas só se tornaram mais práticas nos últimos 100 anos, com o surgimento das máquinas de escrever e, depois, dos computadores. E, com elas, vieram novas dores no pescoço.

4. Trabalhe os flexores profundos do pescoço

Como hoje passamos muitas horas do dia olhando para telas, Ghosh explica que fortalecer a resistência dos músculos flexores do pescoço pode ser útil. Esse grupo de músculos contribui para a estabilidade do pescoço e ajuda a sustentar o peso da cabeça.

Para exercitar os flexores do pescoço, deite-se na cama com os joelhos dobrados e os pés apoiados no colchão, e aproxime o queixo do peito.

Coloque uma das mãos atrás da cabeça e levante-a cerca de 2,5 centímetros da superfície da cama. Em seguida, retire a mão e mantenha a posição pelo maior tempo que conseguir. No início, tente permanecer assim por alguns segundos, mas procure aumentar gradualmente até chegar a 30 segundos, se conseguir.

5. Aumente a resistência dos flexores do pescoço

Outra maneira de exercitar ativamente os flexores do pescoço é usar uma cadeira com apoio para a cabeça.

Sente-se na cadeira, olhando para a frente, e empurre a cabeça para trás contra o apoio antes de levar o queixo em direção ao peito. Mantenha a posição por alguns instantes e volte à posição inicial. Repita o movimento algumas vezes.

Uma forma mais avançada de fazer o mesmo exercício é usar uma faixa elástica de resistência. Primeiro, prenda a faixa a um objeto na altura da cabeça. Segure a faixa e passe-a ao redor da testa. Em seguida, dê alguns passos para a frente para esticá-la o suficiente para sentir uma certa tensão. Fique em pé, com a postura ereta, e flexione o pescoço, levando a cabeça para baixo. Faça uma breve pausa, relaxe o pescoço e volte à posição inicial. Repita o exercício.

Com o tempo, esses exercícios podem ajudar a tornar o pescoço mais resistente às exigências da vida no século 21.

articles.summary: O corpo do indígena desaparecido no Rio São Francisco foi localizado em Porto da Folha após três dias de buscas intensas com apoio da aldeia Xokó.
articles.body:
Corpo de indígena desaparecido no Rio São Francisco em SE é encontrado — Foto: CBMSE

O corpo de um homem de 40 anos, que estava desaparecido há cerca de três dias, foi localizado no Rio São Francisco, na região da Ilha de São Pedro, em Porto da Folha , neste domingo (11).

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros Militar de Sergipe (CBMSE), trata-se de um homem indígena. Populares informaram que ele havia saído para pescar com arpão na manhã da última quinta-feira, por volta das 7h, e não retornou.

A corporação foi acionada no mesmo dia, e as buscas foram realizadas pela equipe de mergulho do Grupamento de Busca e Salvamento (GBS).

Durante a operação, o cacique Bá, representante da aldeia indígena Xokó, e outros indígenas auxiliaram nas buscas, utilizando quatro embarcações para apoiar os trabalhos das equipes de resgate.

Na manhã deste domingo (11), após o corpo ser avistado por pescadores, os militares realizaram o resgate. A Criminalística e o Instituto Médico Legal (IML) foram acionados. A causa e as circunstâncias da morte serão investigadas.

Em caso de emergência, a população deve acionar os bombeiros pelo telefone 193.

articles.body:

Um homem de 25 anos foi encontrado morto dentro de casa na noite deste sábado (10) em Barrolândia , região central do Tocantins. A companheira da vítima relatou aos policiais que estava em um dos quartos do imóvel quando ouviu gritos e, em seguida, disparos de arma de fogo.

De acordo com a Polícia Militar (PM), a equipe foi acionada por volta das 23h10 para uma ocorrência com disparos na Vila Ribeiro. Os militares encontraram o jovem caído no chão, aparentemente sem sinais vitais. A mulher informou que estava no quarto e não presenciou o crime.

O g1 questionou a identidade da vítima à Secretaria de Segurança Pública, mas até a última atualização desta reportagem não obteve retorno

A Perícia Científica e o Instituto Médico Legal (IML) foram chamados para realizar os trabalhos técnicos e fazer a remoção do corpo.

Ainda conforme a PM, as circunstâncias do homicídio serão investigadas pela Polícia Civil. Até o momento, nenhum suspeito foi preso.

Com o crime registrado em Barrolândia, o Tocantins atingiu a marca de seis homicídios contabilizados em um intervalo de seis dias. A sequência teve início na segunda-feira (5) na capital. Keginaldo Primo dos Santos, de 33 anos, que atuava na equipe de limpeza do Hospital Geral de Palmas (HGP), foi assassinado a tiros no setor Morada do Sol 3, após criminosos armados invadirem a residência onde ele morava.

Na quarta-feira (7), outros dois homicídios ocorreram no estado. Também no setor Aureny III, em Palmas, o técnico de enfermagem João Matheus Aguiar Souza, de 26 anos, foi morto a tiros quando retornava para casa. No mesmo dia, durante a tarde, um homem ainda não identificado foi baleado em Araguaína , chegou a receber atendimento do Samu, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos.

Na noite de sexta-feira (9), dois crimes foram registrados. Em Palmas, Welington Alves Costa, de 18 anos, foi morto a tiros dentro de uma barbearia no setor Jardim Aureny III. Pouco depois, em Araguaína, Josias Martins Oliveira, de 29 anos, foi assassinado a golpes de arma branca no setor Araguaína Sul IV, onde foi encontrado caído na rua com diversos ferimentos.

Todas as ocorrências seguem sob investigação da Polícia Civil e nenhum suspeito foi preso até o momento.

articles.title: Best pre-gym drinks that help manage weight
articles.summary: Go to any gym.
articles.body: Go to any gym. You will see people holding all kinds of pre-workout drinks, some with bright colors, some made at home, and some straight from a supplement container. When it comes to actually helping with weight management, not every pre-gym drink is effective. Research in exercise physiology and metabolism has found an option that really help both by making workouts better and by helping the body burn fat and control hunger.Black CoffeeCoffee is one of the studied pre-workout drinks, and for a good reason. Studies that appear in sports nutrition publications have found that caffeine makes the body use fat as fuel during exercise, a process called fat oxidation. Research has also shown caffeine can slightly increase the metabolic rate for hours after being consumed, often called its thermogenic effect. Along with the metabolic benefits, caffeine has been shown to make exercise easier and reduce the feeling of effort, meaning workouts feel a little easier, which can lead to people working harder or longer without stress.Green TeaGreen tea gives an option that is better than coffee while still having real research behind it. Studies have found that green tea has catechins, a compound called EGCG, which works with the natural caffeine in green tea to help burn fat during exercise. Several studies have linked drinking tea regularly to small improvements in body shape over time, especially when combined with regular exercise. Unlike coffee, green tea has caffeine, which makes it a good choice for people who are sensitive to strong stimulants.Water with LemonIt sounds too simple to make a difference. Research on hydration shows that even a little dehydration can make exercise harder and slow down the metabolism. A body that is well hydrated is better at burning calories and controlling hunger. Some research has also found that drinking water before meals or before a workout can slightly lower how many calories are eaten later, probably because the body sometimes mixes up thirst and hunger signals. Adding lemon does not help burn a lot, but it does help people drink more water if they don't like plain water.Black coffee with a little milk and cinnamonBased on the research about caffeine already talked about, some studies have looked closely at the role of cinnamon in controlling blood sugar. Research has found that cinnamon can help the body use insulin better, making blood sugar control around workout time which can help keep energy levels steady and reduce cravings after a workout. A small amount of milk adds some protein, which some research suggests can help reduce hunger without adding calories before training.Beetroot JuiceBeetroot juice has become very popular in sports science research because of its high nitrate content, which the body turns into an oxide, a substance that improves blood flow and how much oxygen reaches working muscles. Many studies have found that beetroot juice can make exercise longer and be more efficient, allowing people to work harder or longer, which helps burn more calories over time. None of these drinks act like a solution, for losing weight on their own. What the research consistently shows is that they help with workouts, better fat burning and better energy and hunger control three things that when added to regular exercise and a good diet really help create real results over time.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Masonry from Perth's lost monastery may have been reused for drain
articles.summary: Archaeologists hope to uncover more fragments of the medieval site in Perth.
articles.body:
Surviving parts of a monastery set up by King James I of Scotland almost 470 years ago may have been found in an old drain.

The Charterhouse was established in Perth for monks of the Carthusian Order , and at the heart of the complex was a lavishly decorated church.

The monastery was later demolished and over the centuries the medieval site disappeared under a hospital and houses.

During an excavation last month, archaeologists and volunteers uncovered an 18th Century culvert that appeared to have been partly made using stone from the torn down monastery.

Listen to news from Tayside and Central on BBC Sounds

The culvert once drained waste water from King James VI Hospital, which was built around 1749-1750 and was converted into flats in the 1970s.

The drain was discovered during the dig in a grassy open space at the former hospital.

Covering the top of the drain were flat stones, which are believed to be medieval masonry.

Archaeologist Dr Gavin Lindsay told BBC Scotland News: "You can see clear chisel marks from when they had been worked very carefully to create these beautiful smooth sides.

"They are clearly far more elaborate, and far more effort had gone into their production, than you would do for a drain in the 1700s."

The selection of masonry also include stone floor slabs.

Dr Lindsay said a stone mason who visited the dig suggested the slabs' smooth surfaces were the result of people walking on them over many years.

"Possibly by many monks' feet, and to push it a bit further, maybe King James's feet had been across it," said the archaeologist.

Dr Lucy Dean, of the University of Highlands and Islands Centre for History, is also involved in the Perth Charterhouse Project.

She said: "The volunteers that we had did a lot of sifting through the soil that we were taking out.

"They were finding, alongside quite a lot of 19th and 20th Century pieces of pottery and glass, a number of pieces that are probably medieval."

The stones from the drain along with fragments of pottery will be examined further by specialists.

The archaeologists said the next stages of the project included studies of archives to find out more about the monastery, and going back to the local community to let them know what has been found so far.

Further digs could take place in the future.

Residents of Perth have also been asked to look out for more masonry that had survived and been reused.

Dr Lindsay said: "We have identified a number of different fragments that have been incorporated into the retaining wall of Perth Station, for example, and into boundary walls of gardens."

The University of Stirling and Perthshire Society of Natural Science have been involved in the project, while funding for the dig was provided by the trustees of the King James VI Hospital and The Guildry Incorporation of Perth.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV to have surgery after nodule found on lung
articles.summary: The 71-year-old pontiff said the nodule was identified "at a very early stage".
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV has announced he will be operated "in the coming days" after a nodule was found on his lung during a medical check up.

"The doctors found an early, well-localised nodule on my lung," he told the public during his weekly Sunday prayers in St Peter's Square in Rome.

The 71-year-old pontiff said his medical team "believe it would be right to intervene" and he had agreed to the operation.

Pope Leo reassured pilgrims that the mass was "well-contained" and caught "at an early stage".

He concluded his Angelus prayer by thanking everyone for their "spiritual closeness" and said he entrusted himself to their prayers.

Holy See Press Office spokesperson Matteo Bruni told the media that "the operation is scheduled for the first days of next week".

Bruni added that the Pope is expected to take about a week to recover.

Vatican News, the Holy See's news portal, said the operation will take place at Gemelli Hospital in Rome.

The hospital set up a special Papal suite following the failed assassination attempt on Pope John Paul II's life in May 1981, which is still in use today.

Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed her "personal solidarity" to the Pope in a post on X as he "faces the ordeal ahead in the coming days".

She was echoed by Italian President Sergio Mattarella, who offered "my sincerest wishes for a peaceful recovery and a speedy and full return to health".

Isaac Herzog, the president of Israel, also wished the pontiff "a full and speedy recovery".

Pope Leo, born Robert Francis Provost, succeeded Pope Francis in 2025 . He is the 267th occupant of the throne of St Peter – and is the first American.

He was ordained in 1982 and spent years as a missionary in Peru, where he is remembered as a figure who worked with marginalised communities.

During Sunday's service, the Pope confirmed his visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru in November will still go ahead.

The Archbishop of Montevideo, Daniel Sturla, said preparations for the pontiff's visit will continue with "greater enthusiasm" as he called for prayers for his recovery.

According to the National Health Service, a lung nodule is a small lump of tissue that is usually detected following an X-ray or CT scan of the chest.

Most nodules are do not cause other symptoms.

articles.title: Comedian Ron Bennington Recalls Early Symptoms of Stage 4 Colon Cancer: ‘Sick As I’ve Ever Been’
articles.summary: For about a month earlier this year, comedian and longtime radio personality Ron Bennington had never felt more ill in his life.
articles.body: For about a month earlier this year, comedian and longtime radio personality Ron Bennington had never felt more ill in his life. “I was as sick as I’ve ever been,” the 67-year-old tells TODAY.com. “I couldn’t hold any food down, and it was like a ridiculous amount of pain and vomiting.” For weeks, he pushed off going to the doctor, he says. “(I was) thinking maybe if we just have a popsicle, everything will be fine, some juice.” Finally, in March, Bennington contacted a local healthcare provider, who suggested a CAT scan. The next day, he got a call advising him to go to the hospital or emergency room. “I go, ‘Why?’ He goes, ‘Maybe there’s a little blockage. I don’t know.’ And as soon as I was in there, I was being operated on within a half an hour later, and the whole thing changed. And then the next morning, they said this is not curable,” Bennington recalls. He got his Stage 4 colon cancer diagnosis while going back and forth to Florida for vacation, which was “really relaxing,” he jokes. But the truth is he wasn’t upset when he received the news. “My initial thing was gratitude for the life that I lived, and I was actually telling the doctor, ‘Look, I understand that you’re upset telling me this ... but I’m fine. I’m great.’ I just immediately thought, ‘What a wonderful life I’ve had,’” he says. “I know the funniest people in the world. I’ve interviewed everybody that I grew up being in love with. I have a wonderful family and a wonderful wife, and everything I got away with. I never worked a day in my life ever — bad student, bad employee, and somehow people say, ‘Just come back, do it again.’” Looking back, Bennington says it was “insane” of him not to seek medical care for so long because of how much pain he was in. But given his history, it wasn’t surprising. “I never went to a doctor once in my life, and it worked out decade after decade,” he jokes, adding that he believes men are afraid of seeming “sick.” The only demographic that may be even more afraid of hospitals? Comics, Bennington says. It’s a phenomenon he’s seen play out first hand while recording his new podcast, “Portcast” on SiriusXM, where he interviews fellow comedians during his chemo treatments in New York City. So far, Michael Che, Shane Gillis, Stavros Halkias and Jessica Kirson have been featured. New episodes come out every Tuesday. Bennington expects to continue chemotherapy for the rest of his life, and he’s also taking a clinical trial drug. “I try to do everything that they ask of me. People say ‘fight’ — fight how?” he quips. “If somebody came in here named Cancer, I’d knock them out. Now, I just try to take my medicine when they tell me to and eat right. That’s it.” The hope is that the treatments give him more time, but he says he’s “OK with everything that happens.” Reflecting on his diagnosis, Bennington says he wants people to understand how quickly their lives can change, and that your health challenges affect more than just you. “Anything can change a family in a New York minute,” he says. “I want to remember that this happens to all of us together.” One of the goal’s for “Portcast” is to encourage people to stay on top of their health by showing the power of open conversations, says Dr. Mark Pochapin, host of SiriusXM’s “Doctor Radio” and gastroenterologist at NYU Langone. “The American psyche is you go to a doctor when you’re sick, we need to change that,” he explains. “You go to a doctor when you’re well to stay well.”

articles.title: What caused Nana Patekar’s death? Autopsy points to blood clot in major heart artery
articles.summary: PANAJI: Actor Nana Patekar died of a heart attack after a blood clot blocked the left main coronary artery, which supplies blood to a large part of the
articles.body: PANAJI: Actor Nana Patekar died of a heart attack after a blood clot blocked the left main coronary artery, which supplies blood to a large part of the heart, according to his autopsy report, a senior doctor at the state-run Goa Medical College and Hospital (GMCH) said on Sunday.The postmortem confirmed the cause of death as “acute myocardial infarction due to left main coronary artery thrombosis secondary to atherosclerotic occlusive coronary artery disease, a natural cause of death”, news agency PTI reported.The 75-year-old actor was rushed to a private hospital from his home in Dona Paula, near Panaji, in the early hours of October 8.His caretaker had approached the hospital seeking an ambulance, saying Patekar was unwell. The ambulance was sent to his apartment, located within a kilometre of the hospital.Doctors administered cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) for 45 minutes, but Patekar could not be revived. He was declared dead at 5.10am, with a doctor suspecting a heart attack.His mortal remains were subsequently taken to GMCH for an autopsy. Patekar's son, Malhar, arrived in Goa to take his father's body back.It was taken to Pune before being transported to the family's farmhouse in Donje village, where the actor was cremated with full state honours.Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar, Union ministers Ramdas Athawale and Murlidhar Mohol, Lok Sabha MP Sunil Tatkare, NAAM Foundation co-founder and actor Makarand Anaspure, FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, actor Jackie Shroff and several other personalities from Bollywood, politics and sports attended the funeral.(With inputs from PTI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Goa | Silver Rate in Goa | Bank Holidays in Goa | Public Holidays in Goa | Petrol Price in GoaStay updated with the latest Goa news. articles.title: Nursing student found hanging in Katihar rented room
articles.summary: 20-year-old nursing student Ankit Kumar Mandal found hanging in rented room in Katihar; police and FSL investigating, body sent for post-mortem.
articles.body: Patna: A 20-year-old nursing student was found hanging in his rented room in Katihar district late Saturday night. Police are probing the circumstances surrounding his death. A fellow student told police that he had not attended college for about two months and had been worried about his studies.The deceased was identified as Ankit Kumar Mandal, son of Omprakash Mandal and a resident of Sikti block in Araria district. Since Feb 2026, he had been staying at the house of Kalicharan Mandal in Bengali Colony under Sahayak police station area. He was studying at a private nursing college near Katihar Medical College.According to police, Ankit’s friend and fellow student Ajay Kumar Mandal went to his room around 11.30pm on Saturday to call him for dinner. When repeated knocks went unanswered, Ajay alerted the land owner. A Dial 112 police team reached the spot and broke open the door. Ankit was found hanging inside the room.Land owner Purnima Sarkar said, “Ankit had cooked and eaten his meal on the night of Oct 9, leaving the used utensils in the kitchen. He returned to his room on the morning of Oct 10 after staying out through the night.”She said she was sweeping the house when Ankit returned. He quietly went into his room and shut the door.Ajay told police that Ankit had not been attending college for around two months. He also claimed that Ankit had failed his first-semester examination and was worried about his studies. However, police have not officially confirmed academic stress as the reason behind the death.A team from Sahayak police station inspected the spot, while forensic science laboratory (FSL) personnel examined the room and collected evidence. The body was sent to Katihar Sadar Hospital for post-mortem.Sahayak police station SHO Kumar Vikash said, “The family has reached Katihar. We could not yet question them as they are in mourning. articles.title: Silent inflammation could be damaging your body — and 5 habits may help keep it in check
articles.summary: Jim LaValle reveals how the gut-immune-brain interface drives chronic inflammation, and why stress, blood sugar and environmental toxins play key roles.
articles.body: Inflammation is a natural immune response that helps protect the body from injury and infection, but when it becomes chronic, it can pose a health threat, according to the National Institutes of Health. Over time, chronic inflammation can contribute to rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, inflammatory bowel disease and cardiovascular disease. Keeping the condition in check can help protect healthy tissues and support overall health, experts say. POPULAR WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS MAY HELP PROTECT AGAINST A DEADLY DISEASE, DOCTOR SAYS Jim LaValle, a clinical pharmacist and metabolic medicine expert based in Texas, told Fox News Digital that inflammation can be influenced by a variety of factors beyond injury or infection. LaValle first pointed to the gut-immune-brain connection — the communication between gut microbes, the immune system and the central nervous system — as one pathway that can influence the body's inflammatory response. Beyond gut health, he said several everyday lifestyle factors can play a role in preventing chronic inflammation. DOCTORS SAY 8 FORGOTTEN HABITS COULD HELP FIGHT STRESS, OBESITY AND CHRONIC DISEASE No. 1: Manage stress Managing stress and anxiety can help support the gut-brain connection and keep inflammation in check, according to LaValle. He pointed to cortisol, a hormone released in response to stress, which he said can "wreak havoc on your chemistry" when levels remain elevated. Chronic stress can also affect the intestinal barrier, potentially allowing substances that would normally remain inside the gut to pass through more easily, LaValle said. This increased intestinal permeability is sometimes called "leaky gut." ZERO SUGAR, MORE PROBLEMS? STUDY REVEALS SURPRISING GUT HEALTH EFFECTS "So, it turns out that if I'm stressed out a lot, I can be more prone to irritable bowel," LaValle said, as stress can trigger or worsen digestive symptoms in some people. No. 2: Watch for food triggers Diets high in sugar, fat and ultraprocessed foods can also affect gut health. Paying attention to which foods trigger certain symptoms may help identify potential food sensitivities or intolerances, LaValle noted. Symptoms such as bloating, rashes or discomfort after eating certain foods may signal a food-related reaction, although they can have other causes. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Certain medications, including antibiotics, may also alter the gut microbiome, but their effects vary depending on the drug and the individual, the expert said. No. 3: Keep blood sugar in check Maintaining healthy blood sugar levels is another important factor in managing inflammation, according to LaValle. LaValle noted that conditions such as diabetes and insulin resistance are often associated with chronic inflammation. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Research suggests that GLP-1 medications, commonly prescribed for type 2 diabetes and obesity, may have anti-inflammatory effects, while scientists are investigating other potential benefits beyond weight loss and blood sugar control. No. 4: Be aware of environmental exposures The "exposome," or the environmental exposures people experience throughout their lives, can influence inflammation and the risk of chronic disease, according to the National Institutes of Health. LaValle pointed to emerging research on how environmental exposures — including "forever chemicals," microplastics, metals and pesticides — may affect weight, blood sugar regulation and other aspects of health. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "A lot of us don't think about that kind of impact on our health and how that could trigger inflammation signaling," he added. No. 5: Don’t over-train Regular exercise supports overall health, but intense workouts without adequate recovery time can put additional stress on the body, LaValle cautioned. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "You’re not getting a good enough recovery," he said. "You’re training hard. And, in fact, you might be training hard every day to lower that cortisol, but you're not getting good recovery. And that could lead to silent inflammatory signaling as well." Anyone who is concerned about chronic inflammation or is experiencing persistent symptoms should consult a doctor to determine the underlying cause and appropriate treatment.

articles.title: Efferon wants to eradicate the devastating toll of pediatric sepsis
articles.summary: This Battlefield 200 startup has developed blood-purification tech to save children
articles.body:
Sepsis, an acute inflammation triggered by infection, is a leading cause of childhood mortality, claiming roughly 3 million children under the age of five annually.

Efferon , a startup selected as one of TechCrunch Disrupt 2026’s Startup Battlefield 200 , is on a mission to drastically lower that number.

The company has developed a medical device that it says lowers organ failure rates and significantly accelerates recovery in children.

When standard treatments like antibiotics cannot stop the immune system’s overreaction, a patient’s blood must be filtered to remove deadly toxins. That is where Efferon’s devices, of absorbers of dangerous cytokines and toxins, step in to make a critical difference.

Dima Romashin, Efferon’s co-founder and CEO, compares what happens in the body during sepsis to a fire, where an immune response overwhelms the body rapidly. “In a fire, there are two things: the flame itself and smoke that it produces,” he told TechCrunch.

In sepsis, endotoxins are the flames and cytokines are the smoke. Efferon, unlike other devices on the market, has developed a mechanism that can absorb both at once, according to Romashin.

Although Efferon makes absorbers for adults, Efferon NEO, its pediatric device developed specifically for young kids, is proving especially effective. Since children have a significantly lower circulating blood volume, they require medical devices engineered specifically for their physiology, according to Romashin.

In April, Efferon NEO received a CE mark , Europe’s equivalent to FDA approval, making it the first multimodal blood purification device specifically engineered for pediatric sepsis.

Efferon NEO is used in intensive care units across 30 countries, including European hospitals, Saudi Arabia, and Thailand. The company is now preparing to file for FDA approval and is on track to hit $2 million in annualized revenue by the end of 2026.

The startup’s technology was originally developed by scientists at Moscow State University, including co-founder Ivan Bessonov. Recognizing its potential, Romashin, a serial entrepreneur, stepped in earlier this year as CEO to help commercialize it.

Although Romashin admits that Efferon isn’t growing at the breakneck pace of today’s AI startups, true success for the company is measured by something else entirely: every child who gets to go home.

articles.title: Innocent mistake on long flight could have devastating consequences for travelers
articles.summary: One traveler was diagnosed with a corneal ulcer after wearing contact lenses all throughout an 11-hour flight — prompting eye doctors to warn about cabin air risks.
articles.body: An everyday habit during a long-haul flight could have painful consequences for certain travelers — with a recent case highlighting some serious dangers. The dry air inside an airplane cabin, combined with hours spent wearing contact lenses during a long travel day, can leave the lenses with less moisture and eyes feeling increasingly uncomfortable, experts say. In some cases, irritation or damage to the surface of the eye can lead to more serious problems. FLIGHT ATTENDANTS BEG TRAVELERS TO STOP DOING THE ONE THING THAT ANNOYS CREWS MOST One traveler recently described temporarily losing vision in one eye after returning home from an international trip, according to the New York Post. The woman said she wore her contact lenses throughout an 11-hour flight home from Greece and for roughly 24 hours of travel — while also wearing them while swimming and showering, according to the outlet. Within days of returning home, the traveler developed pain and sensitivity to light before her vision significantly worsened. Doctors eventually diagnosed her with a corneal ulcer. She underwent weeks of treatment with eye drops and was left with a small scar that continues to blur part of her vision, the outlet reported. The traveler developed pain and sensitivity to light before her vision significantly worsened. Valerie Kattouf, an Illinois-based optometrist, told Fox News Digital that wearing contacts during extended flights can increase dry-eye symptoms and lead to irritation, a "sandy, gritty feeling" and intermittent blurred vision. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "The cabin air has significantly reduced humidity that can actually remove moisture from the contact lens and create more dryness," Kattouf said. Falling asleep during a long or overnight flight can add another concern for travelers wearing contacts. "People often sleep on long flights, which contributes to more risk with contact [lens] wear," Kattouf said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES As a contact lens loses moisture, it may move less freely on the eye, Kattouf said. Removing a particularly dry lens could potentially disturb the epithelium, the outer layer of the cornea, causing significant irritation and potentially affecting vision. For travelers preparing for a long flight, Kattouf recommends bringing an up-to-date pair of prescription glasses. "Wearing glasses during a long flight is more ideal for eye health and long-term comfortable contact [lens] wear," she said. As another option, travelers who begin their journey wearing contacts can switch to glasses before sleeping or partway through the flight, Kattouf suggested. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ For those who keep their contacts in, single-use vials of artificial tears may also help provide additional lubrication during the flight, according to Kattouf. The issue has also led to discussion among travelers online, with some saying they routinely opt for glasses during longer trips. "I [always] wear glasses on long flights," one Reddit user wrote. "My eyes just feel so much more comfortable by the time I land, and I don't have to worry about taking them out at the airport or on the plane, or sleeping on the plane." "My eyes were so dry at the end, even with eyedrops," the person wrote.

articles.title: What to know about Pope Leo’s lung surgery
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV said Sunday he will have surgery this week to remove an early-stage nodule on his lung.
articles.body: Pope Leo XIV said Sunday he will have surgery this week to remove an early-stage nodule on his lung. The Vatican didn’t say what type of lung surgery the pontiff will undergo, but that the “small, localized nodule” was found in his lung during recent medical tests. A lung nodule is a small mass of tissue detected through X-ray or CT scan screening. According to the American Lung Cancer, nodules can be caused by a number of factors, including irritants such as air pollution, diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and cancer. They can also be caused by scar tissue from a previous infection. Leo said the nodule was detected “at a very early stage.” There are several approaches to surgery, depending on the size and location of the nodule and whether doctors suspect cancer, said Dr. Ankit Bharat, the chief of thoracic surgery at Northwestern Medicine. Most nodules are benign, and it’s unclear whether the pope had a biopsy after the tests. “When doctors decide to proceed directly to surgery rather than first obtaining a biopsy, it can suggest a higher level of concern on the lung scan,” Bharat said. Lung cancer is more treatable if caught early. The deadly cancer is most often caused by cigarette smoking, but about 20% of lung cancer cases are diagnosed in people who have never smoked or used tobacco, according to the American Cancer Society. However, finding a nodule on a scan doesn’t confirm a cancer diagnosis, Bharat said, and the surgery will reveal more information as doctors are able to put the nodule under a microscope. Advances in the procedures mean they are generally less invasive and some patients begin walking within a day or two. Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni said in a statement Sunday that “the operation is scheduled for the first days of this week and the estimated post-operative recovery time will be about one week.” If the nodule is larger and more lung tissue is removed, meaning the surgery is more extensive, it may be three to four weeks before a patient is fully recovered. “Given the pope’s age, his recovery could be slower than that of a younger, otherwise healthy patient,” Bharat said. Leo is 71. The pontiff has a major trip scheduled to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru in November. It’s possible he could make the trip, doctors suggest, if the surgery is minimally invasive and there are no surprise findings. If the nodule is cancerous, doctors will determine whether he can be treated while traveling or the trip may need to be postponed.

articles.title: Preocupación por David Alonso: trasladado al hospital tras grave caída en el GP de Indonesia
articles.standfirst: David Alonso sufre contusión pulmonar en el GP de Indonesia de Moto2: parte médico tras el accidente
articles.summary: David Alonso sufre contusión pulmonar en el GP de Indonesia de Moto2: parte médico tras el accidente
articles.body: DEl Gran Premio de Indonesia disputado en el Circuito Urbano Internacional de Mandalika dejó un balance agridulce para el motociclismo nacional. David Alonso, representante de Colombia en la categoría intermedia de Moto2, sufrió una dura caída apenas iniciada la competencia que lo obligó a abandonar y a ser trasladado de urgencia a un centro médico. El joven corredor del equipo CFMoto Aspar Team había logrado clasificar en la tercera posición de la grilla de salida, proyectándose como uno de los candidatos firmes a pelear por la victoria en la isla de Lombok. Sin embargo, al encarar la primera curva del trazado, un choque múltiple en el que se vieron involucrados cuatro pilotos provocó la neutralización inmediata de la prueba mediante bandera roja. Debido al fuerte impacto recibido en la maniobra, Alonso se retiró visiblemente afectado e invadido por el llanto. Poco después, las asistencias médicas del circuito determinaron su traslado a un hospital cercano para descartar complicaciones internas. A través de sus canales oficiales, el Aspar Team dio tranquilidad a los aficionados al emitir el parte médico sobre la salud del piloto: "El colombiano no ha podido participar en la reanudación de la carrera. Alonso ha tenido que ser trasladado al hospital por una contusión pulmonar y se han descartado otras lesiones." A pesar del susto e impacto de la maniobra, los exámenes médicos descartaron fracturas u otros daños de gravedad adicionales a la contusión en la zona pulmonar. Este incidente en Lombok representa la segunda competencia que pierde Alonso en lo que va de la temporada, tras no haber competido previamente en el Gran Premio de Tailandia. En su segundo año disputando la categoría de Moto2, el corredor cuenta con un balance positivo de una victoria (obtenida en los Países Bajos) y dos podios más (tercer puesto tanto en Aragón como en Austria). El abandono sin sumar puntos tuvo consecuencias directas en la tabla general de pilotos: A la espera de su evolución médica y posterior alta para retomar entrenamientos de alta intensidad, el calendario del Mundial de Motociclismo marca que la próxima salida a pista de Moto2 tendrá lugar entre el 23 y el 25 de octubre, cuando se corra el Gran Premio de Australia

articles.title: 300 held for CJP stir on Day 2 in Mumbai, let off after UBT & MNS youth netas hit the ground
articles.summary: Mumbai Police detained around 300 at Shivaji Park during a CJP protest over alleged electoral fraud; Aaditya and Amit Thackeray intervened, warning statewide agitation from Oct 12.
articles.body: Mumbai: Around 300 people were detained on Sunday as they began to gather at Dadar’s Shivaji Park for Cockroach Janta Party’s protest over alleged electoral fraud for the second consecutive day. They were released after Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Aaditya Thackeray, his brother Tejas and their cousin MNS’s Amit Thackeray intervened with an impromptu sit-in along with scores of supporters near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar. The Thackerays warned that protests across the state would intensify from Monday.Police said they were in the process of filing an FIR over the Shivaji Park stir for unlawful assembly.“If police seal one location, we will agitate elsewhere,” Aaditya told reporters after the detainees were released. “This is an undeclared Emergency. Any of us could be arrested any time. It’s not just students but other citizens who are agitating. It is BJP versus Bharat. The agitation will continue till chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns,” he said.MNS said it had intimated police that a protest will be held at Shivaji Park at 4pm on Monday. Aaditya said the details of the agitation will be shared on X. “It is our responsibility to provide you with a safe space,” he said.Amit said he was taking a walk in the evening when he saw police stopping young people. “Have they converted Shivaji Park into a war zone? What kind of way is this to rule the state and country? I’m going to come here every day. Let them detain me,” he said.Aaditya said the Centre had put more forces in Delhi than it had during the Kargil war. “Why is BSF in Delhi, deployed against Indian citizens?” he asked.CJP and left-wing organisations had called for a protest at 4pm at Shivaji Park on Sunday. Police deployed heavy security at Dadar Metro station and Dadar railway station to prevent protesters from gathering near gate 6, close to the statue of Meenatai Thackeray. All roads leading to the entrance were barricaded as a precautionary measure. Shetkari Kamgar Paksh leader Samya Korde was also placed under house arrest. Some residents said police blocked the entrances of their buildings to prevent them from going for the protest.As the crowd began to swell from the afternoon, police began to detain people. Many protesters alleged that people were dragged away and bundled into police vans. Among those detained was social activist Anjali Damania, who said the country is facing an undeclared Emergency. “I have been held at Tardeo police station. What is our crime? Can’t we say anything against govt?” she said on X. “Supreme Court has stated that the right to a completely peaceful movement cannot be stopped. Mumbai police should watch this video. The right to conduct peaceful movements exists in democracy. How can they pick us up like this?”A 25-year-old protester suffered a panic attack while in detention at Tardeo police station and was rushed to Nair Hospital. “He was taken to the hospital and has since been released from the police station,” said a police official.Around 600 were detained for turning up for a protest at August Kranti Maidan on Saturday and were released later.
